claims.text: Applying a stable low-friction surface coating to a refractory high-entropy alloy substrate will decouple bulk mechanical properties from surface tribological behavior.
The coated refractory high-entropy alloy will provide self-lubrication across a wide temperature range.
A refractory high-entropy alloy can provide excellent mechanical strength at ambient and elevated temperatures.
The refractory high-entropy alloy substrate has high-temperature stability.
Uncoated refractory high-entropy alloys lack adequate intrinsic self-lubricating behavior.
Chemical vapor deposition can be used to incorporate a stable h-BN or similar lubricious phase on the refractory high-entropy alloy substrate.
The intervention will produce a coherent engineered coating or tribofilm.
The engineered coating or tribofilm will provide low friction.
The engineered coating or tribofilm will protect the refractory high-entropy alloy substrate.
The coating reduces direct metal-to-metal contact during sliding.
The coating maintains its lubricious properties over a wide temperature range, including oxidative conditions.
The underlying refractory high-entropy alloy can sustain mechanical loads at elevated temperature.
Compared with an uncoated refractory high-entropy alloy, the coated material will have significantly lower friction coefficients across diverse temperatures.
Compared with an uncoated refractory high-entropy alloy, the coated material will have significantly lower wear rates across diverse temperatures.
Adding the coating will not compromise the alloy's high-temperature strength and stability.
Coating decomposition, delamination, or chemical reaction with the substrate under extreme or cyclic thermal loading may degrade performance.
The long-term thermal stability and adhesion of the proposed coating under thermal cycling and reactive environments are not fully established.
